clue.text: Cole takes luggage in taxi close to Braintree

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
a bag is a piece of luggage

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of Braintree is used

explanation.surface: A man named Cole loads his bags into a cab heading towards the Essex town of Braintree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cole' looks like a person's name but is an old word for the brassica family. 'takes' and 'in' just link the pieces; Braintree is a town in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is an old and dialect name for brassicas, the vegetable group that includes the common garden cabbage.

clue.text: Poet and author held by commies in revolution

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside it, so the writer goes within the other piece
a revolution turns something right round, so the communists are read backwards

parts.note: commies, like reds, is a slang word for communists
pen is used for a writer, as in a poison pen

explanation.surface: A poet and a novelist are taken prisoner by communist rebels during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' reads the communists backwards (SDER), and 'held by' puts the writer within. 'Poet' is the definition, not part of the wordplay, though the surface makes all three sound like people.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was an English poet of the 1930s generation alongside Auden and MacNeice.

clue.text: Compound tainted iced tea brought round before noon

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are brought round the other piece, enclosing it
tainted tea has been spoiled or corrupted, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means the morning hours before noon

explanation.surface: Someone finds that a cup of iced tea brought to them in the morning has been contaminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tainted' rearranges ICED TEA into ACETIDE, and 'brought round' wraps those letters about AM, giving ACET-AM-IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetamide is a simple organic chemical substance, the amide derived from acetic acid.

clue.text: Last from Monkhouse joke stock

indicators.note: the last from a word is its final letter, here the end of the comedian's surname

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A comedian's final gag comes from his standard stock of material.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Monkhouse was a British comedian and game-show host famous for one-liners, which makes the 'joke stock' picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock a kitchen or workshop is to furnish or supply it with what it needs.

clue.text: Place in Surrey for one overacting

parts.note: eg, exempli gratia, means for example, or for one
a ham is an actor who overacts, and ham acting is overacting

explanation.surface: A Surrey town is singled out as an example of theatrical overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham is a town in the English county of Surrey, near Runnymede on the River Thames.

clue.text: 17 hero giving attention to basketwork

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay them attention
wicker is woven willow used in baskets

explanation.surface: The hero of a famous book listens closely to someone weaving baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' just links. 17 is the clue for Joyce's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker, the tavern keeper HCE, is the central figure of James Joyce's final novel.

clue.text: Award winner — first clue here?

parts.note: a victor is a winner
the first clue in this crossword is 1 across, with the one written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Is this, the first clue in the puzzle, about a man who won a medal?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cryptic definition of the medal itself, but it is a charade: the opening clue of any grid is 1 across, read as I ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military decoration for gallantry in the face of the enemy.

clue.text: Agnes soused with pub wife appears in spurious comic work

indicators.note: the combined letters appear inside the other word, splitting it open

parts.note: something spurious is fake, not genuine
an inn is a pub

indicators.note: soused means drunk, so the name is reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken woman named Agnes and the landlord's wife turn up in a bogus comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soused' gives EGANS from the name; 'appears in' sets the string inside the word for spurious. 'comic work' fits a novel famed for its puns.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnegans Wake is James Joyce's famously playful, punning novel, full of comic wordplay.

clue.text: Practised catches in the grass

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
to catch what someone says is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone rehearsing their lines is overheard while hiding in long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'the grass' must be one specific grass, the reed, rather than lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rehearsed something is to have practised it beforehand, as with a play or speech.

clue.text: Soldiers after charge can't stand

indicators.note: the soldiers come after the charge in the answer

parts.note: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a criminal charge in British law
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers facing a charge on the battlefield are unable to hold their ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a military attack, but it is a legal charge here.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest it, so you cannot stand it at all.

clue.text: Choice between stem and stern for Argonaut needing a vessel

indicators.note: the choice word sits between the first and last letters
a ship's stem is its front and stern its back, so the first and last letters of the word are taken

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Argonaut must choose between the bow and the stern of his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship words pun on the Argonauts sailing the Argo, but stem and stern are just the ends of the word: A and T, with OR set between.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, and a blood vessel is a tube carrying blood.

clue.text: Benefit to collect towards ESA mentioned above

indicators.note: the help collects the other letters, taking them inside

parts.note: aid is help or benefit
for can mean towards, as in heading for home
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes to pick up a welfare payment, the ESA mentioned earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: ESA is the UK Employment and Support Allowance, a state benefit, which drives the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a formal word for already referred to earlier in a document or speech.

clue.text: Shocking fuss accompanies outside broadcast

parts.note: to make a scene is to make a fuss

explanation.surface: A row breaks out during a live television transmission from a location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanies' only links the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is offensive and outrageous, the sort of thing that shocks people.

clue.text: Like a bald tyre, maybe, sons twice pulled out, rocking lever

indicators.note: the two letters are pulled out of the longer word

parts.note: a bald tyre has lost its tread, so it could be described as treadless

indicators.note: twice asks for the letter to be given two times over

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mechanic with worn tyres and two sons rocks a lever back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out' removes both S letters from TREADLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated pedal lever rocked to drive a machine such as a sewing machine.

clue.text: Husband in robe left here to worship

indicators.note: the husband goes inside the robe

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak, a kind of robe

explanation.surface: A husband in his robe left for a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H inside CAPE, giving C-H-APE, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small building or room set aside for Christian services and prayer.

clue.text: He composed second letter, spelled out later to preserve old volume

parts.note: the second letter of the alphabet written in full as a word

indicators.note: the time word preserves the others by holding them inside

parts.note: then can mean afterwards or later

explanation.surface: A composer writes a second letter, spelled in full later, to keep an old book safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to preserve' has the time word hold O and V. 'second letter, spelled out' means the letter's name written as a word, not the letter itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig van Beethoven was the great German composer of nine symphonies, so he composed music.

clue.text: Weak in recession, I intend to block account

indicators.note: the reversed letters block the account by sitting in its middle
recession is going backwards, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: I intend can be said as I mean

explanation.surface: During an economic downturn, someone plans to freeze a feeble bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' gives NAEMI, and 'to block' sets it inside the account. 'recession' sounds economic, beside 'account', but only signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic, from a lack of red blood cells, has come to mean pale, feeble or lacking vigour.

clue.text: Drink consuming Australian Harry, racketeer, rising writer

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the whole string is reversed
the drink consumes the other piece, taking it inside

parts.note: ale is a drink
Oz is slang for Australia and Australian
Harry Lime is the racketeer in the film The Third Man

explanation.surface: A racketeer called Harry, drinking with an Australian, makes his name as a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' gives ALOZE, and in a down clue 'rising' reads everything upwards. Harry Lime is the black-marketeer of the 1949 film The Third Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was the French novelist of the Rougon-Macquart cycle and author of J'accuse.

clue.text: Fine cut for commentators

indicators.note: commentators speak, so the word is as they would say it

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with sheep

explanation.surface: Sports commentators announce that a fine is being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for commentators' signals a word as spoken: SHEAR is said like SHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is fine and very thin, almost transparent.

clue.text: English-Gaelic translation written in couplets

indicators.note: a translation changes words into a new form, so the language's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English rendering of a Gaelic poem is set out in pairs of rhyming lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' gives LEGIAC from the language. Elegiac couplets are the classical metre of elegy, pairing a hexameter with a pentameter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac verse is classically composed in elegiac couplets, alternating hexameter and pentameter lines.

clue.text: Soak or submerge to negotiate river

indicators.note: to negotiate an obstacle is to get round it, so the dipping word goes round the river

parts.note: to dunk is to dip or submerge

explanation.surface: Someone must either soak or plunge themselves in order to cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' just links. 'to negotiate' has DUNK go round R, giving D-R-UNK. 'Soak' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A soak is slang for a heavy drinker, someone habitually drunk, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Run public house in time, and situate vacant couch differently

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the pub letters go inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
PH is the abbreviation for public house, used on maps

indicators.note: a vacant word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A pub landlord who runs the place moves an empty sofa around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PH into ERA, giving E-PH-RA; 'vacant' empties SITUATE to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch a statement is to express it in words, so to couch it differently is to put it another way.

clue.text: Batting team dismissed completely

parts.note: a side that is batting in cricket is said to be in
a side is a team
a dismissed batsman is out

explanation.surface: A cricket team is bowled out in full while batting.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket terms give the pieces: a batting side is 'in', and a dismissed batter is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is to know it thoroughly, so the phrase means completely.

clue.text: Being out, have order picked up by neighbours?

indicators.note: letters that are out are out of place, so these are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Neighbours listen in on someone told to obey an order while they are out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being out' rearranges HAVE ORDER. The question mark marks the definition as an example: neighbours may pick up through the wall what they were not meant to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overheard has been heard by people it was not meant for, such as those next door.

clue.text: Stressed command of tzar so muddled

indicators.note: muddled means confused or jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tsar's order was so confused that it caused stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' rearranges OF TZAR SO. 'command' suggests a ruler's order, but it is a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sforzato is a musical instruction telling the performer to play a note with sudden strong accent.

clue.text: East Sea creature sheds tail in Spring

indicators.note: to shed a tail is to lose the final letter

parts.note: the manatee is a large marine mammal, the sea cow

explanation.surface: In springtime, a sea cow off the east coast loses its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheds tail' removes the last E of MANATEE. 'Spring' looks like the season but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or spring forth from a source.

clue.text: Answer arrived about extremely discursive intellectual world

indicators.note: the arrival word goes about the extreme letters, enclosing them

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An answer turned up that rambled at great length about the scholarly world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the ends of 'discursive' inside the verb; 'extremely' looks like an intensifier but picks the extremes, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of universities, scholarship and learning.

clue.text: Spanner's good held by new union member

indicators.note: the good letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: a bride is a newly joined partner in the union of marriage

explanation.surface: A newly married woman holds on to a good spanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' suggests a tool, but it means something that spans; 'union' suggests a trade union but is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge spans a river or road, so it is literally a spanner.

clue.text: Cross-country runners from Gosforth are slower

indicators.note: the answer comes from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Runners from a district of Newcastle turn out to be the slower ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Gosforth is a district of Newcastle upon Tyne. In the paper-chase game of hare and hounds, the hares are the runners who lay the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: In hare and hounds cross-country races, the hares run ahead laying a trail for others to follow.

clue.text: Apparition in relative darkness

definitions.meaning: a ghost or spirit of the dead
an area sheltered from direct sunlight

explanation.surface: A ghost lurks in the semi-darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shade means both a ghost of the underworld and an area dimmer than its sunlit surroundings.
